prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aims
- End austerity with a responsible fiscal plan, fair taxation and investment in public services.
- Protect family incomes and social security; tackle inequality and low pay.
- Keep Scotland in the European Single Market and ensure Scotland’s voice in Brexit.
- Uphold Scotland’s right to choose its future, including an independence referendum mandate.
- Modernise UK democracy (proportional representation, votes at 16, abolish House of Lords) and scrap Trident.

Record since 2015
- Opposed austerity, forced U‑turns on tax credit and disability cuts; led campaigns against the two‑child cap and “rape clause.”
- Backed WASPI women; passed the Istanbul Convention Bill on ending violence against women.
- Challenged punitive benefit sanctions; opposed bombing Syria; led anti‑Trident case.
- Exposed misuse of Scottish Limited Partnerships; secured veterans’ compensation parity.
- Defended individuals in unfair immigration cases.

Scottish Government achievements
- Record NHS investment; free prescriptions; best-performing A&E in UK; integrated health and social care.
- Expanded free childcare; free university tuition; rising exam passes; record apprenticeships.
- Lower council tax, free personal care, highest UK housebuilding rate, higher youth employment, highest Living Wage coverage, more police and lowest crime in 42 years, no Bedroom Tax.

Fiscal and tax plan
- Balance the current budget by 2021/22; debt falling from 2019/20; release ~£120bn UK-wide for services.
- UK-wide 50p top rate; oppose VAT/NI rises; reverse married couple’s allowance and bank levy cuts; tax bankers’ bonuses; improve tax collection and transparency.

Public services and NHS
- Increase NHS Scotland budget by £2bn; pass through all consequentials; oppose privatisation in England; support an NHS Reinstatement Bill.
- Prioritise mental health, workforce pay, safe staffing, EMA/EHIC continuity, PrEP access, EMA membership and medicines regulation continuity.

Education and young people
- Childcare to 30 hours for 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; targeted attainment funding; no grammar schools; protect free tuition; restore Post‑Study Work Visa; safeguard EU research and Erasmus.

Jobs, pay and workers’ rights
- No further corporation tax cuts; double Employment Allowance; extend Annual Investment Allowance.
- Raise Minimum Wage to real Living Wage over the Parliament; repeal Trade Union Act; ban exploitative zero‑hours; close gender pay gap; fair public sector pay.

Brexit and constitutional
- Demand Scotland’s place at the negotiating table and Single Market membership.
- Strengthen Holyrood with repatriated and additional powers (agriculture, fisheries, environment, employment law, immigration, trade agreements).
- Defend human rights (ECHR, Human Rights Act) and seek Sewel consent on Brexit bills.

Economy, industry and infrastructure
- Support oil and gas (exploration, late‑life assets, decommissioning, diversification); protect sector in Brexit talks.
- Invest in roads, rail (devolve Network Rail; connect to HS2), broadband to 100% by 2021, housing, and city/regional deals (UK to match Scottish funding).
- Back small business cashflow, late payment protections, phased digital tax reporting.

Rural, food and fisheries
- Return £190m convergence uplift to farmers; oppose funding/power grabs; maintain Single Market access; protect EU workers; secure GIs for Scottish products; devolve fisheries fully.

Democracy, defence and security
- PR for Commons; abolish Lords; strengthen Electoral Commission; reform lobbying law.
- Scrap Trident; invest in conventional defence, protect Scottish bases and shipbuilding; maintain Europol cooperation; better veteran support; tighten arms export controls.

Environment and energy
- Champion low-cost renewables (onshore/offshore wind, wave/tidal), island interconnectors, storage, and CCS; reform punitive grid charges; oppose Hinkley; match Scotland’s climate ambition; oppose fox hunting.

International and refugees
- Keep 0.7% aid; climate justice; ethical trade; LGBTI envoy; reopen Dubs scheme; fairer asylum with right to work after 6 months; end indefinite detention; improve housing and integration.
